_spec.purpose: A standalone web edition of the archived visual story.
_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: West Texas A&M won a USDA grant for a research feedlot near Canyon. The release says new methods can be tested with AI and names no tool, vendor or result.

introduction.text: [West Texas A&M University has received a {{money:c1}} grant from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which the A&M System's release calls the largest federal award in the university's history](c1). [The grant comes through USDA's Research Facilities Act Program for a center for beef cattle research and innovation](c2).

[The release says new feeding, health and handling techniques can be evaluated with traditional and artificial intelligence-powered approaches](c6). That sentence is the release's only mention of AI. [It names no AI tool, vendor, camera, model or result](c7).

paragraphs.text: [A required dollar for dollar match, ${{number:c3}} million from the A&M System and another ${{number:c3:1}} million from other sources, brings the project total to ${{number:c3:2}} million](c3). [The release says the Texas Cattle Feeders Association, its members, university donors and other sources will match the System's share](c13).

[The research feedlot pairs {{number:c4}} small research pens for scientific studies with {{number:c4:1}} commercial-scale pens](c4). [Plans call for a precision beef cattle handling facility, a veterinary care and research hospital, an advanced technology feed and production center and a metabolism and physiology center](c5). The release describes these as planned components. None is described as built.

[Ground was broken in November {{number:c8}} next to WT's Nance Ranch](c8). [The ranch lies about seven miles east of Canyon, covers {{number:c9}} acres including its headquarters and was given to WT in {{number:c9:1}}](c9). [Brothers and Canyon ranchers Mike and Gary Kuhlman gave {{number:c10:1}} acres beside the ranch in {{number:c10}}](c10).
[The release ties the work to WT's Center for Advancing Food Animal Production in the Panhandle and its Feedlot Research Group](c16).

[USDA's Cattle on Feed report estimated {{number:c17:2}} thousand head on feed in Texas's large feedlots on September 1st](c17). [Nebraska had {{number:c19:2}} thousand](c19) [and Kansas {{number:c18:2}} thousand](c18). [The national total was {{number:c20:2}} thousand](c20).

[The release says AI-powered approaches are designed to increase beef production efficiency and advance feedlot management practices](c7). It does not say which tools the feedlot will test, who will supply them, what they will measure or when any result will be published. A reader can't tell from the release whether AI work has begun or remains a plan for the finished pens.
